description.value: The study examined how perceptual salience and categorical salience at different levels of abstraction jointly influence categorization behavior and frontoparietal BOLD activity.

design.value: Subjects performed a visual random-dot-motion categorization task during four fMRI sessions. Motion coherence and motion direction relative to an oblique category boundary were independently varied, and behavioral data were modeled with a proportional-rate diffusion model while BOLD responses were analyzed with voxelwise general linear models, parametric contrasts, ANOVAs, ROI analyses, and BOLD time-course estimation.

description.value: Accuracy on the leftward-versus-rightward motion categorization task.
Time to make the button-press categorization response.

source_definition.value: Perceptual salience was manipulated via the introduction of noise into motion coherence; salience decreased as motion coherence decreased.

type.value: categorical factor with parametric linear trend

levels.value: 0%, 25%, 100%, and 1 intermediate coherence (IC) ranging from 12% to 15%; two subjects were assigned two IC values because they over- and underperformed at 25% coherence.

source_definition.value: Categorical salience was manipulated by varying the direction of motion of the dots: salience decreased as the coherently moving dots moved closer to the boundary line.

type.value: categorical factor with parametric linear trend

levels.value: 0°, ID, 45°, 90° - ID, and 90°; ID ranged from 8° to 20°.

name.value: motion coherence × distance from category boundary

source_definition.value: A three-way mixed-effects ANOVA used coherence and distance from boundary as fixed factors and subjects as a random factor; the diffusion-model regression used motion coherence, distance from category boundary, and their interaction as independent variables.
Subjects were included as the random factor in the three-way mixed-effects ANOVA.
Parametric weights corresponding to accuracies at different stimulus combinations were applied to the stimulus regressors.

description.value: Ten subjects, ages 18–42 yr; 4 men and 8 women, participated in the study and gave written informed consent. All subjects had normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist, were right-handed, and had normal or corrected-to-normal vision.

inclusion_criteria.value: Normal neural anatomy as assessed by a neurologist

exclusion_criteria.value: A high percentage of aborted trials; responding outside the response window in >20% of trials within each run in two scanner sessions

description.value: One subject was excluded from both the behavioral and imaging analyses; nine subjects remained for analysis.

task_description.value: Subjects viewed a variable proportion of coherently moving dots on a background of randomly moving dots and categorized the direction of motion as either leftward or rightward of an oblique category boundary. The boundary was presented for 5 s at the start of each block; each trial began with fixation, followed by a 2.5-s random-dot kinematogram and a jittered 2–12-s intertrial interval.

instructions.value: Subjects were instructed to report their choice via a button press as quickly and accurately as possible, using the index or middle finger of their right hand. They were instructed to pay attention to the entire field of dots.

stimuli.value: A random dot kinematogram with variable proportions of coherently moving and randomly moving dots. Dots moved in one of 16 directions; dot density was 16.7 dots·°−2·s−1, dot velocity was 5°/s, and the presented images subtended a visual angle of 7.5°.

task_performance_measures.value: aborted trials, defined as trials in which subjects did not respond within the allotted duration

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner at the Henry H. Wheeler, Jr. Brain Imaging Center at the University of California, Berkeley; 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Functional images consisted of 32 slices acquired with a single-shot gradient echoplanar imaging protocol in a contiguous order.

instrument.value: Siemens MAGNETOM Trio 3-T MR scanner; 12-channel phased-array coil

description.value: Anatomical images consisted of 160 slices acquired with a T1-weighted MP-RAGE protocol.

fMRI preprocessing included conversion to four-dimensional NIfTI format, slice-timing correction, motion correction, spatial smoothing, fMRI-to-structural coregistration, warping of the anatomical image to functional-image space, and normalization to the MNI_N27 standard volume.

steps.value: Functional images were converted to four-dimensional NIfTI format.
Images were corrected for slice timing offsets.
Motion correction was carried out with AFNI 3dvolreg, using the mean image of the first run in the series as the reference volume.
Images were smoothed with a 5-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
Coregistration was performed with AFNI 3dAllineate using the local Pearson correlation cost function for fMRI-to-MRI structural alignment.
The inverse transformation was used to warp the anatomical image to functional image space.
Anatomical images were normalized with FSL fnirt to the MNI_N27 standard volume.
The same normalization parameters were applied to native-space statistical maps as necessary for group statistical maps.

model_settings.value: The Palmer model consisted of A′, the decision threshold; x, stimulus salience; k, a proportionality constant linking stimulus salience to drift rate μ (μ = kx); and TR, mean residual time in seconds. Three versions were implemented: an Interaction model with 20 x values and one each of A′, k, and TR; a Distance model with x determined by categorical distance and A′, k, and TR fit for each distance; and a Coherence model with x determined by motion coherence and A′, k, and TR fit for each coherence. Corrected Akaike information criterion was used for model comparison.

estimator.value: An iterative procedure designed to optimize the log-likelihood of the diffusion-model fit; the best k was found for each combination of A′ and TR, followed by selection of the best-fitting A′, k, and TR.

hrf_model.value: gamma probability density function peaking at 6 s

model_settings.value: Voxelwise fMRI statistical analyses were performed for each subject. The four coherence values and five unique distance values were modeled with separate regressors. Tests of linear trends used vectors transformed to zero mean with a sum of squares equal to 1 and applied the weights to the estimated beta coefficients. Only correct trials were evaluated except for the accuracy map.

estimator.value: Voxelwise estimation in the general linear model framework

model_type.value: group-level voxelwise analysis and mixed-effects ANOVA

model_settings.value: Subject-level maps were mapped to the MNI template and subjected to group-level analyses. An ANOVA used motion coherence and distance from boundary as fixed factors and subjects as a random factor.

estimator.value: Mixed-effects ANOVA with subjects as a random factor

hrf_model.value: piecewise B-spline basis functions separated by 100-ms intervals for 20 s after onset

model_settings.value: Hemodynamic responses starting at stimulus onset were estimated for each combination of motion coherence and distance from category boundary. Peak amplitude was defined as the first maximum after stimulus onset, and time to peak was the time from onset to this maximum.

description.value: No coherent motion signal; dots moved randomly.
One intermediate coherence ranging from 12% to 15%; two subjects used alternative intermediate coherence values of 4% or 10% or 25% or 35% as specified by individual performance.
Dot motion was along the category boundary, providing minimal categorical salience.
An intermediate distance between 0° and ±45°, ranging from 8° to 20°.
Dot motion was 45° from the category boundary.
An intermediate distance between ±45° and ±90°, defined as ±(90° - ID).
Dot motion was maximally distant from the category boundary and therefore had high categorical salience.

name.value: negative parametric effect distance from category boundary

definition.value: Tests of linear trends were carried out for each voxel using the distance from category boundary vector transformed to zero mean and a sum of squares equal to 1.

multiple_comparison_method.value: cluster size correction derived from the AFNI programs 3dFWHMx and 3dClustSim

interpretations.value: BOLD activity increased with decreasing categorical salience.
